outcome: Recommend the lifecycle control that best addresses a personnel or contractor security gap.

sections.body: Screening, job descriptions, agreements, orientation, supervision, transfer controls, and termination procedures each address a different lifecycle risk. The organization should define responsibilities, acceptable-use and confidentiality obligations, access approval, return of assets, and timely revocation. Controls must respect law, contracts, privacy, and the role’s actual risk rather than applying an arbitrary one-size-fits-all process.
keyPoints: A transfer requires removal as well as new access.
Offboarding must account for accounts, devices, credentials, knowledge transfer, and assets.
sections.title: Security follows the relationship

sections.body: Vendors, consultants, and contractors may hold data, administer systems, or enter facilities without being employees. Agreements should define scope, security requirements, confidentiality, reporting, monitoring, access lifecycle, subcontracting conditions, and exit obligations. A business sponsor and service owner need to remain accountable for the relationship; procurement alone cannot operate the security control.
keyPoints: Contract language must be supported by onboarding, monitoring, and offboarding practice.
Third-party access is a lifecycle, not a permanent badge.
sections.title: Extend controls to nonemployees

sections.body: Candidate screening and hiring should be proportional, authorized, consistent, and tied to role sensitivity. Employment agreements and policy-driven requirements establish confidentiality, acceptable use, intellectual-property, reporting, and sanctions expectations. Onboarding, transfer, and termination processes must create, change, review, or remove access, assets, duties, training, and acknowledgements promptly. Vendor, consultant, and contractor agreements must define scope, access, supervision, confidentiality, return or destruction, incident notice, and offboarding. Failure modes include orphaned access, unacknowledged obligations, bypassed screening, and suppliers treated as employees without equivalent contractual controls.
keyPoints: Name the accountable owner, decision criterion, and evidence for each applicable outline topic.
Record the failure consequence and escalation or review trigger rather than assuming a policy label proves operation.
sections.title: Apply personnel controls across employee and third-party lifecycles

sections.body: Personnel screening, agreements, monitoring, sanctions, and offboarding must be authorized, consistent, proportionate to the role, and aligned with labor, privacy, contract, and anti-discrimination obligations. Define the role sensitivity, permitted screening/monitoring basis, decision owner, evidence minimization and retention, appeal/escalation route, and trigger for re-screening or access review. An employment agreement or acknowledgment establishes obligations such as confidentiality, acceptable use, intellectual property, reporting, and sanctions only when it is valid and communicated under the applicable regime. Over-collection, inconsistent screening, or using an agreement as a substitute for access lifecycle controls creates legal, privacy, and security failures.
keyPoints: Risk-sensitive roles may justify stronger controls, but not an unlimited right to collect or monitor.
Keep personnel evidence limited to the authorized purpose and retention period.
A signed agreement does not itself revoke access or return assets at transfer or termination.
sections.title: Apply personnel controls under local authority and role risk

workedExamples.takeaway: The identity persists, but access must follow the current relationship.

workedExamples.reasoning: The sponsor defines privileged duties and required screening/contract clauses with HR, procurement, privacy, and counsel as applicable. Before access, verify the authorized engagement, confidentiality and acceptable-use terms, identity, role-based approvals, training, sponsor, expiry date, monitoring rules, and return/offboarding plan. Revalidate at renewal and remove access when work ends.
